description: We are Shackleton Sight, two UMA students in Málaga (Mechanical & Industrial DesignEng. + Telecom Eng. & Maths) tackling Challenge Lunar Landing Site Navigator. We already have the core math & algorithm to process LOLA DEM elevation matrices and compute solar illumination or Earth radio Line-of-Sight.
summary:
Where do you park a lunar lander when the Sun skims the horizon and mountains block Earth's signal? 
🛰️🌑 Lunar Landing Navigator solves the Lunar South Pole's toughest engineering puzzle! Using real NASA JPL DE421 ephemerides and LOLA elevation maps, we built an interactive 3D digital twin that calculates exact horizon shadows, partial solar disk eclipses, optimal fixed-panel azimuths ☀️, and Earth telecom link budgets (FSPL in S/X/Ka bands, signal delay, and libration) for any future mission🚀. Switch seamlessly between Educational Mode 🎓 and Engineer Mode 🛠️ to compare sites, crown the #1 landing spot with our Viability Ranking 🏆, and export instant mission reports!
details:
What it does & How it works 🚀🌕 Lunar Landing Navigator is an interactive, full-stack digital twin built for planning lunar surface missions—like Artemis, VIPER, and CLPS—at the Moon's South Pole. You simply plug in any landing coordinates, mast or antenna height (from 0.1 m up to 100 m), and a UTC mission window (spanning 1900 to 2053). Under the hood, our physics engine crunches 360° topographic horizon profiles accounting for the Moon's spherical curvature, partial solar disk occlusion, zero-refraction vacuum ephemerides, solar energy generation, and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) radio link metrics.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact 💡🛰️ Landing at the Lunar South Pole is the ultimate engineering balancing act: crater floors hide valuable water ice but trap landers in freezing darkness and Earth signal blackouts, while crater rims bask in near-eternal sunlight over treacherous terrain. Our tool bridges the gap between public outreach and real mission planning with two synchronized interfaces running on the exact same physics engine:

  • Educational Mode 🎓: Built for students and space fans, featuring real rover height presets (from a 0.5 m micro-rover to a 3.5 m Artemis tower), an interactive shadow compass, and crystal-clear connectivity indicators.
  • Engineer Mode 🛠️: Unlocks custom mast heights, optimal azimuth search for fixed vertical solar panels, DTE pointing angles (Az/El), lunar libration spans, light-time latency (OWLT/RTT), Free-Space Path Loss (FSPL) across S, X, and Ka bands, "Golden Window" hours (simultaneous Sun + Earth visibility), a weighted Viability Ranking (0–100 pts) for Artemis, ISRU, and Comms profiles, plus downloadable CSV/PDF mission reports.

Tech Stack & Tools 💻⚙️

  • Backend: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Skyfield (powered by official NASA JPL DE421 ephemerides), NumPy, and Pytest (backed by 58 automated physics and API oracle tests).
  • Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js / React Three Fiber (for our interactive 3D Lunar Globe, 360° Sky Dome, and LOLA 3D terrain), and Vitest (8 automated frontend tests).
  • Quality Assurance: A custom AST contract parity auditor running 62 automated checks to keep our Python and TypeScript data schemas 100% in sync.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered ✨🔭 Instead of relying on basic "on/off" sunlight guesses, we modeled real partial solar disk occlusion, spherical lunar curvature across 50–100 km ray casts, and zero atmospheric refraction. Even better, we engineered an azimuth optimizer for fixed vertical solar arrays to capture the South Pole's super-low solar elevation angles.
